key_terms.الْمُحْرِمَ: The one in Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram use henna?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that henna is permissible for the Muhrim because it is categorized as a medicinal substance or general adornment rather than a specific 'perfume' (thayb) whose scent is the primary intent. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between prohibited scents and permissible natural substances used for healing or decoration during Hajj and Umrah. The ruling reflects the practical application of legal principles where the essence of the substance, not just its origin, determines its status.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Henna. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the one in Ihraaam, let him touch it and heal his camel with it, and it is not a perfume, and there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 17. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about henna (privet). He (the Imam) said, ‘A person in the state of Ihram can touch and treat his camel with it. It is not a perfume and it is not harmful.’”
